prompt: A candle burns at a constant rate. After $2$ hours it is $18$ cm tall, and after $5$ hours it is $10.5$ cm tall. What was the height of the candle, in centimeters, before it was lit?
hint: Constant rate means a linear model. Find the rate first.

hints.text: Constant rate means a linear model. Find the rate first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try an easier pair: after $1$ hour a candle is $9$ cm and after $2$ hours it is $7$ cm, so it burns $2$ cm per hour. Running back one hour from the 9 cm mark gives $11$ cm at the start.
It lost $18 - 10.5 = 7.5$ cm over $3$ hours, so it burns $2.5$ cm per hour.
Run back $2$ hours from the 18 cm mark: $18 + 2(2.5) = 23$ cm.

learningObjective: Extrapolate a linear model backwards to its initial value.
explanation: A constant burning rate means height is a linear function of time. The rate is $\dfrac{10.5 - 18}{5 - 2} = \dfrac{-7.5}{3} = -2.5$ cm per hour.
The phrase before it was lit means time $0$, which is $2$ hours earlier than the reading of $18$ cm.
Going back in time undoes the burning, so add $2$ hours of burning to that reading: $18 + 2(2.5) = 23$.
The candle was $23$ cm tall before it was lit.

alternativeExplanations.title: Write the equation
steps: The rate is $\dfrac{10.5 - 18}{5 - 2} = -2.5$ cm per hour, so through the point $(2, 18)$ the height is $h = -2.5(t - 2) + 18$.
Distribute and combine to put it in slope-intercept form: $h = -2.5t + 5 + 18 = -2.5t + 23$.
Before the candle was lit means $t = 0$, and the equation gives a height of $23$ cm there.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Subtracting the two hours of burning gives $18 - 5 = 13$ cm, and stopping at the first reading gives $18$ cm, and both are wrong.
Before it was lit the candle had to be taller than at any later reading, so the answer must be more than $18$.
Adding back the $2 \times 2.5 = 5$ cm burned in the first two hours gives $18 + 5 = 23$ cm.
